previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, and gastroparesis was admitted after her mother found her unresponsive and hypothermic. She had experienced nausea and headache the prior day, ate only breakfast, and took her usual long-acting insulin, leading to severe hypoglycemia with a blood glucose of 25. She was treated with glucagon and IV dextrose, warmed with a bear hugger, and stabilized. She missed a dialysis session, contributing to fluid overload and hypertension, and underwent hemodialysis during admission. Her blood sugar fluctuated but stabilized on her home insulin regimen. Abdominal pain was attributed to chronic gastroparesis, and mild pulmonary congestion resolved. She improved clinically, regained mental clarity, tolerated oral intake, and was discharged home with instructions to continue her medications, attend dialysis, and follow up with her endocrinologist.

# MSSA bacteremia with right wrist and hip pain:
Pt. presented with right wrist and hip pain. Given notable 
edema, erythema, and warmth of the right wrist, ortho was 
consulted to aspirate the joint.  This revealed only 280 WBCs on 
cell count. Pt was started empirically on vancomycin and zosyn 
for presumed cellulitis. The following day, blood cultures 
showed MSSA, and pt was narrowed to cefazolin. Still with 
swelling ___ the wrist, she was taken for washout with Ortho on 
___. She was found to have purulence around the wrist tendon 
sheath with cultures also growing MSSA. The right hip, which had 
also been bothering the patient, was tapped at that time as 
well, though from the hip cultures had no growth. Subsequently, 
the pt underwent transthoracic echo showing no vegetation. The 
suspected source of her bacteremia was recently placed L 
indwelling portacath.  Given that pt. has extremely difficult 
access frequently requiring central lines as well as frequent 
admissions, the decision was made ___ conjunction with infectious 
disease team to leave the portacath ___ place with antibiotic 
locks ___ addition to systemic antibiotics.  Pt overall improved 
and her wrist pain had mostly resolved by discharge.  
Unfortunately she continued to have hip pain.  MRI on ___ did 
not show any evidence of fluid collection, osteo, or fracture.  
She was discharged home with the following plan for antibiotics: 
cefazolin post-HD for 6 weeks total and vanc-sodium citrate 
locks changed every 48hrs at the ___ 4 
weeks total.  She will continue to be followed by infectious 
disease ___ the ___ clinic.

# C diff infection:
Pt had loose stools on the ___ night of her stay, prompting c 
diff testing. These were positive, and pt. was started on po 
vanc and transitioned to po flagyl once clinically improved. She 
will need to continue this through the course of her IV 
antibiotics.

blood stream infection. However, it resolved with IV antibiotic 
treatment before further workup could be performed.

INDICATION:  ___ year old woman with ESRD on HD and MSSA bacteremia with severe

TECHNIQUE:  An MRI of the right hip was performed utilizing the following
sequences on a 1.5 Tesla magnet with a cardiac coil:  Large field of view
coronal STIR and T1 of the entire pelvis and oblique axial, sagittal and
coronal fat saturated proton density of the left hip.

COMPARISON:
Radiographs of the right hip and pelvis ___.

FINDINGS: 

Bone marrow signal is within normal limits for the patient's age without
evidence for osteomyelitis, fracture, or avascular necrosis.

No hip joint effusion is detected on either side. There is no evidence of a
displaced labral tear on this limited exam in the absence of administered
intra-articular contrast.  No paralabral cyst is seen.

There is diffuse, symmetric intramuscular edema involving the of the pelvic
girdle muscles and muscles of the proximal lower extremities bilaterally.

A fluid collection is not seen.

The visualized tendons are normal in appearance including the hamstring
origins and gluteal tendons.

Articular cartilage is maintained at the hips bilaterally. The sacroiliac
joint spaces are maintained. There is mild, nonspecific asymmetric edema about
the right sacroiliac joint.  No joint effusion is seen. There is no evidence

Limited assessment of the lower lumbar spine is grossly unremarkable.

Limited evaluation of the pelvic viscera demonstrates no gross abnormality on
this nondedicated exam.  There are slightly enlarged bilateral inguinal lymph
nodes measuring up to 1.2 cm in short axis dimension, nonspecific in etiology.
There is a moderate amount of free fluid within the pelvis.

There is diffuse subcutaneous soft tissue edema.  Intermediate signal material
seen about the right hip joint (05:11, 06:12) appears to represent mildly
edematous fat (03:20) and is seen bilaterally.

IMPRESSION: 

1. No evidence of fracture, femoral head osteonecrosis, or femoral acetabular
joint effusion.  Diffuse anasarca. Although no contrast was administered,
there is no obvious focal fluid collection to suggest abscess.

3. Mild asymmetric edema about the right sacroiliac joint. If the patient has
pain localizing to the right sacroiliac joint, further evaluation can be
obtained with dedicated sacroiliac MRI, as the differential diagnosis could
include sacroiliitis.

4. Nonspecific diffuse, symmetric intramuscular edema involving the pelvic
girdle and proximal lower extremity muscles.
